One ASCENDING index serves both the Active (validUntil asc, filtered '>') and Expired (validUntil desc, filtered '<=') queries — Firestore can scan a composite index in either direction.
Reports/Payments: revenue by method within a date range (paid).
Reports/Payments: refunds/failed/GST within a date range (status + createdAt).

Payments header line: this-month Paid revenue (status + createdAt range + sum(amount)). A sum() aggregate needs the summed field in the composite index — the plain status+createdAt index above does not cover it (confirmed live via the FAILED_PRECONDITION index-creation link Firestore returns for this exact query shape).

Payments: all-time Paid revenue total (status + sum(amount), no date bound). Same sum()-needs-the-summed-field requirement as the month-scoped index above, discovered at the same time — this all-time query was silently failing FAILED_PRECONDITION before this index existed (fetchPaymentStats' Promise.all rejects entirely if any one aggregate query fails, so this alone was enough to zero out the whole stats block).
Payments: all-time Refunded total (status + sum(refundAmount)). Same issue as the two indexes above, for the refunds aggregate.

Reports payment mix (fetchPaymentReport methodAgg): method + status + createdAt range + sum(amount). The method+status+createdAt index above does NOT cover it — every aggregated field must appear in the index, and this query sums `amount`. Verified live: without this, all three method aggregates fail with FAILED_PRECONDITION, which takes down the whole payment report (they share one Promise.all) and renders 'Refund rate 0.0%' from a null result.

Reports refund total (fetchPaymentReport): status == Refunded + createdAt range + sum(refundAmount). The status+refundAmount index above has no createdAt, and status+createdAt has no refundAmount — a ranged sum needs both in one index.
Reports GST collected (fetchPaymentReport): status == Paid + createdAt range + sum(gstAmount). Same shape as the status+createdAt+amount index above, for the other summed field.

recomputeProductRating — count() + average('rating') over a product's PUBLISHED reviews. An aggregation over a field needs that FIELD in the index, so `rating` must be here even though nothing filters or sorts on it; the sibling index above (…, createdAt) does NOT satisfy it. Without this the aggregate throws FAILED_PRECONDITION, onReviewCreate/Update/Delete swallow it, and products keep averageRating 0 / totalReviews 0 no matter how many real reviews are posted.

dailyCleanup (nightly) — active coupons whose validUntil has passed, so they can be deactivated. Equality on isActive + range on validUntil needs this composite; without it the coupon-expiry pass of dailyCleanup dies FAILED_PRECONDITION and lapsed coupons stay redeemable forever.

Wallet 'Rewards received' tile — sum(amount) of a user's credits from one source. `amount` MUST be the last field: a sum()/average() aggregation requires the AGGREGATED field in the index, not just the filtered ones. Without it the query fails FAILED_PRECONDITION and the tile silently reads zero.

Web Batch 4 (D4) — affiliate wallet 'This Month' tile: sum(amount) of one affiliate's Referral credits within the current calendar month (userId ==, source ==, createdAt range). `amount` is the last field because a sum() aggregation requires the aggregated field in the index too (same lesson as the walletTransactions index above) — omitting it fails FAILED_PRECONDITION and the tile would silently read zero.
